P-TARGET-UNDEFINED.because: The target substance or quality variable is not named, so no method can be justified yet
source: AFS ref §3 'Insufficient information can be the right answer'
S01 p.3 (samples of incompletely known composition: test several approaches to select the method)

T-TARGET-PARTIAL.because: Targets are mentioned but not defined as separate variables; each needs its own method check and reference
source: AFS ref D05 ('target variables still need definition')

T-SPLIT-TARGETS.because: Different targets can need different methods; each is assessed on its own
source: AFS ref D05 'target variables still need definition'

T-SPLIT-STREAMS.because: Streams with different optical behaviour need their own interface choice

T-NO-REFERENCE.because: A quantitative result needs an independent reference to build and test a calibration
source: AFS ref §3 (feasibility plan: independent reference measurements)

T-REFERENCE-QUALITY.because: A reference exists, but its uncertainty and sampling time decide what error the spectroscopic model can reach
source: AFS ref D01 (clarification: 'Which assay, uncertainty and sampling time provide the reference concentrations?')

T-PLAN-MINIMUM.because: Go/no-go needs client-agreed acceptance criteria and concentration range; none are invented
source: AFS Q&A 17.10 (lab screening: range, resolution, concentration level)

P-NO-FLUOROPHORE.because: Fluorescence needs a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; most chemicals do not fluoresce

S-FLUOR-INDICATOR.because: An indicator is indirect: the link to the requested variable must be shown against a reference
source: S01 p.16 (NADH, tryptophan, riboflavin as fluorescence targets)

S-UV-NO-CHROMOPHORE.because: UV-Vis needs a defined absorption of the target (biomass trends use turbidity instead, S01 p.16)

S-UV-OVERLAP.because: UV spectra overlap strongly in real mixtures; chemometrics is required

S-WATER.because: Water has -OH bands: overtones in NIR, strong fundamental absorption in MIR
source: S01 p.16 (strong water absorption in IR)

S-VIBRATIONAL-MAJOR.because: NIR and MIR carry composition information (-OH, -NH, -CH groups; MIR fingerprint bands)

S-RAMAN-COMPOSITION.because: Raman gives vibrational composition information (molecular backbone, symmetric groups) for organic components

S-TRACE-NIR.because: NIR may lack sensitivity for components below about 0.1 %

S-AQUEOUS-IR.because: Water absorbs strongly in the infrared; Raman has low water absorbance in comparison

S-AQUEOUS-NIR.because: Water absorbs in the infrared; the materials support NIR in bioprocess only for major components such as glucose or glycerol

S-AQUEOUS-RAMAN.because: Raman suits aqueous media (low water absorbance compared to IR) for metabolites such as glucose, acetate, lactate

S-RAMAN-FLUOR-BG.because: Fluorescence of many organic samples can swamp the weak Raman signal
source: AFS ref D01 ('Check fluorescence background and signal quality')

S-OD-NOT-VIABLE.because: Turbidity correlates with cell density, but optical density is not a viable cell count

I-SAMPLE-TYPE.because: This sample type is not listed for this technique in Table 1 (catalog mapping, see catalog notes); not recommended unless AFS confirms the geometry

I-GAS-OUT-OF-SCOPE.because: No probe in the supplied catalog is a gas interface (Table 1 lists liquid, paste, powder and solid samples)
source: AFS ref §3 (decision status: outside the supported scope)

I-OPAQUE-TRANSMISSION.because: In opaque or thick media light cannot pass the path length; transmission saturates or fails

I-OPAQUE-REFLECTION.because: Diffuse reflection is used for opaque or concentrated dairy products

I-CLEAR-TRANSMISSION.because: Transmission/transflection with 1–10 mm path is preferred for clear liquids

I-CLEAR-REFLECTION.because: Reflection can be less representative for clear liquids

I-OD-VARIES.because: Optical density changes: compare transmission, transflection and reflection on real samples before choosing
source: S01 p.18 (transflection can cover low- and high-fat products)

I-UV-HIGH-OD.because: UV-ATR uses a micrometre evanescent path and works in highly scattering or dark fluids

I-ATR-SURFACE.because: ATR probes only a few micrometres of the surface layer; check that this represents the sample

I-FOULING-CONTACT.because: Deposits on a contact window change the signal; cleaning and access must be agreed

I-PHYSICAL-VARIATION.because: Temperature, texture, particle size and scattering changes can mimic composition changes; separate them in the experiment
source: AFS ref D01 (risks: physical variation of the powder)

P-FIBER-RANGE.because: The fiber does not transmit the method's spectral range (e.g. silica ≤2400 nm, MIR needs 2.5–25 µm)

L-FIBER-PARTIAL.because: The fiber covers only part of the nominal range; state only the usable range of the actual components

L-LINK-LENGTH-MIR.because: Materials show 100–300 m silica Vis-NIR cables but only 2 m example IR fiber cables; a long IR link needs AFS confirmation of length and routing

L-REMOTE-SILICA.because: Silica fibers carry NIR and Raman light over long distances (100–300 m cables), so the analyzer can stand away from the process

L-COMPONENT-RATINGS.because: Temperature, pressure and material ratings of probes are not in the sources; AFS must confirm

L-GMP.because: Pharma installations need GMP and cleaning/sterilisation conditions agreed

P-CALIBRATION.because: A change of API or excipients can invalidate a calibration; a matrix-specific calibration must be built and tested

P-COMBO-NOT-FIX.because: No source shows that adding a method keeps an old calibration valid; a combination is assessed after each single method and its gain is a hypothesis to test

P-SENSITIVITY-NOT-SELECTIVITY.because: High sensitivity is not selectivity; fluorimetry is rated high sensitivity, low selectivity

P-APPROVE-WITHOUT-DATA.because: The concept cannot be approved: a component is incompatible or decisive facts are missing
source: AFS ref §3 'An honest provisional plan is more useful than a final configuration built on missing facts'

P-EXACT-CONFIG-NOW.because: An exact sensor configuration cannot be chosen before the target and the deviation are defined
source: AFS ref §3 'Insufficient information can be the right answer'

P-EVIDENCE-SCOPE.because: A proof-of-concept laboratory study is not proof of readiness for live surgery or production (S03: 14 in vitro samples from 7 patients)

P-CLINICAL-SCOPE.because: Clinical decision use needs in vivo validation on the actual setup; the supplied material is a proof of concept on ex vivo samples
source: AFS ref §3 (decision status: outside the supported scope)

P-ASSET-NOT-EVIDENCE.because: An instrument or cable the client already owns is checked for compatibility; owning it is not evidence of suitability
source: AFS ref §3 'Common mistakes' (missing facts filled in as if given)

P-BUSINESS-SOURCE.because: S05 flyer and S06 link are business context, not evidence of technical performance

APP-PHARMA-BLEND.because: NIR reflection and Raman are used for blend potency in a tablet press feed frame

APP-DAIRY.because: NIR reflection (opaque products) and transmission/transflection (whey, skim milk) are used in-line in dairy

APP-BIO-METABOLITES.because: Raman gives a molecular fingerprint for glucose, acetate or lactate in the same reactor

APP-BIO-NIR-GLUCOSE.because: NIR tracks major components like glucose or glycerol in the millimolar range

APP-BIO-BIOMASS.because: UV/Vis is a low-cost tool for biomass trends because turbidity correlates with cell density

APP-PETRO-WATER.because: MIR ATR probes are shown for water content in petroleum

APP-EXTRUSION.because: NIR reflection and MIR ATR (diamond cone, PIR fiber) are shown for API in hot polymer extrusion

APP-TISSUE-LAB.because: A combined MIR ATR + fluorescence probe separated model tissues in a laboratory study

O-STATUS.because: outside_scope if any case_outside_scope fired; insufficient_information if case_insufficient fired or every non-excluded candidate is needs_info; otherwise provisional. Never 'final'.

O-ORDER.because: Tie-break by S01 Table 1 columns as in `tie_break:` (trace → sensitivity, complex natural media → selectivity, then cost). Only candidates with evidence (application or physics_only) are recommended; rows no rule supports are not shown. Order: evidence application > analogy > physics_only; fewer risk_high, then fewer risks; lower Table 1 cost (simplest sufficient); catalog row id last. Show at most 3 (team choice).
source: AFS Q&A 17.10 ('you don't need a Bentley')
AFS ref D01 'Choose the simplest configuration that meets them'

O-COMBINATION.because: Propose a combination only if listed in the materials and both single methods are in the top-3 of the case; its gain is a hypothesis tested against the best single method; sampling location and acquisition timing of both methods must be aligned (same spot for heterogeneous samples)

O-QUESTIONS.because: Method questions: for each unknown input of a fired or skipped rule, try every value; strength = share of values that change top row, an exclusion or the case status. Strongest first, 5–10 questions in total (Q&A 17.10); plan questions (reference, criteria, range) always, as a separate block.
source: AFS ref §3 'Clarification questions: first the questions whose answers could change the method or the setup'

O-EXPERIMENT.because: Step 0 lab screening of a few samples (range, resolution, concentration level); step 1 representative samples or in-line pilot with independent reference (sampling + lab assay; Q&A examples: chromatography, MS); single methods first, then a listed combination; step 2 held-out validation against client criteria; note: after confirmation the sensor may be reduced to a few wavelengths.

O-SPECTRAL-RANGE.because: A nominal method range is not the range of an instrument, fiber or probe; for Raman state excitation (nm) and shift (cm-1) separately; µm = 10000 / cm-1

O-CITE.because: Every reason carries its source; an AFS page is enough if it directly supports the claim at the same scope (lab/process/clinic); external sources need link and quote
